ours.body: If neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (line 1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so the other collective hosts' calendars are thrown away without any sign. ours.body: The recurring branch now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. For every calendar reference it goes through all of the organizer's calendar credentials and deletes `updBooking.references.find(...)`, which is always the first calendar reference. ours.title: Member calendars without credentialId end up on the organizer's credentials
ours.body: When a pushed team member's `destinationCalendar` has no `credentialId`, `createAllCalendarEvents` takes the else branch (EventManager.ts:376-381). That branch filters `this.calendarCredentials`, which are the organizer's credentials, by integration type, so it creates a second copy of the event in the organizer's calendar instead of the member's. Consider skipping such entries for non-organizer hosts, or resolving that member's credentials.

ours.title: `prisma` is used without an import
ours.body: This file never imports `prisma` (imports at lines 1-20), so this line resolves to the global `prisma`. `packages/prisma/index.ts:56-59` sets `globalThis.prisma` only conditionally (the dev-only hot-reload cache). In production, every Salesforce client construction would then throw a ReferenceError after the token fetch. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

ours.title: Webhook secret compared with `!==`
ours.body: This endpoint can overwrite any user's credentials. The shared secret is checked with plain string inequality, which isn't constant-time. Consider `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers, and reject the request when the header is missing or is an array.

ours.title: Any attendee can make the app email an unlimited list of arbitrary addresses
ours.body: Matching on email alone lets any logged-in user whose email is on a booking (for example someone who booked a public event) add guests, and the guests array has no upper bound (addGuests.schema.ts:5). Every call sends the organizer, team members and every attendee an email from the app's mailer (email-manager.ts:525-549). That is a spam and amplification path. Consider capping `guests` with `.max(...)` and deciding whether attendees should have this permission at all.

ours.title: A stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error stays after a successful add or after closing the dialog
ours.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(false)` runs only in the Cancel handler (line 91). If a submit fails validation, the user corrects it and the add succeeds, `onSuccess` clears the emails but not `isInvalidEmail`, so the next time the dialog opens it shows the error at once. Closing with Esc or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61) also keeps the old emails and the old error. Reset both on success and whenever the dialog closes.

ours.title: Error toast fallback can never run, and it can show 'undefined: …'
ours.body: `message` is a template string and is never empty, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never uses the fallback. When `err.data` is missing (for example a network error), the toast reads `undefined: <raw message>`. Build the code prefix only when `err.data?.code` exists, and fall back to `unable_to_add_guests` when there is no message.

others.text: addGuestsHandler requires user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner (using && instead of ||), blocking team admins who are not owners from adding guests to team bookings

The permission check uses `&&` (AND) instead of `||` (OR). This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously, which is almost never true. A team admin or team owner should each independently have permission to add guests.

Seat bookings need seat-level scoping, but this new action updates by `bookingId` only. On seats events it can add guests to the shared booking instead of the current seat.

`uniqueGuests` only filters against existing booking attendees and the blacklist, but does not deduplicate the input `guests` array itself. Submitting the same email twice in the request will create duplicate attendee records.

ours.body: The cron runs every 15 minutes (`.github/workflows/cron-scheduleSMSReminders.yml:8`). Two failures in a row therefore set `retryCount` to 2, and the next run deletes the reminder, with nothing logged. Failures include a Twilio error or outage, `checkSMSRateLimit` throwing, and `scheduleSMS` returning `undefined` while the user or team is locked (`twilioProvider.ts:90-95`). So an outage of about 30 minutes, or an admin lock that is lifted later, permanently drops reminders for bookings that may b

others.text: In scheduleSMSReminders, the catch block calls prisma.workflowReminder.update() to increment retryCount, but that update can throw if the reminder was deleted concurrently, escaping the catch and aborting the entire cron run

The second OR branch in the deleteMany query deletes ANY WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method type, because it lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing non-SMS reminders (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) to be unintentionally deleted by the SMS cron job

The retryCount is incremented using the stale in-memory value (reminder.retryCount + 1) rather than an atomic database operation. If this cron handler runs concurrently or the same reminder is processed twice, both executions read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing one update. Should use Prisma's atomic increment instead: retryCount: { increment: 1 }
The retry-count cleanup is not scoped to SMS reminders. As written, any reminder with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows

`update()` will throw if the reminder was deleted between `findMany` and this write, which would escape the catch block - needs to be robust to concurrency and missing rows

The deletion query's second OR branch (retryCount: { gt: 1 }) lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so it deletes all workflow reminders with retryCount > 1 including EMAIL reminders, not just SMS reminders

The retryCount > 1 delete condition in deleteMany is missing a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, which could delete workflow reminders of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1, potentially causing silent data loss for non-SMS reminders if another code path increments retryCount

Unguarded DB write inside catch block - if prisma.workflowReminder.update throws (e.g. network issue, record already deleted), the error will propagate out of the catch and abort the entire for loop, leaving subsequent reminders unprocessed

The second OR condition in the delete query lacks the `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, causing the query to delete ALL workflow reminders with `retryCount > 1` regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) instead of only SMS reminders

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` call in the catch block is not wrapped in a try-catch, so if this database update fails the exception bubbles up unhandled, causing the handler to stop processing remaining reminders and the original error to never be logged

The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` call to increment `retryCount` is identically duplicated in two places (when `scheduledSMS` is falsy and in the catch block), risking inconsistent changes if the retry logic needs modification

The second OR clause in the deleteMany query filters only on retryCount > 1 without any method constraint, causing the SMS cron job to delete all WorkflowReminder rows across all methods (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, SMS) that have retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. The fix is to add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the second OR branch.

The prisma.workflowReminder.update in the catch block (line 191) is unprotected - if it throws (e.g., the record was already deleted by the deleteMany above, or a DB connection issue), the error propagates out of the for...of loop and halts processing of all remaining reminders. Wrap this update in a nested try-catch or append .catch() to prevent a single failure from stopping the entire cron job.
The second OR branch in the deleteMany query is missing a method guard, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders - the cleanup should be scoped to SMS only

Using JavaScript-level addition (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of Prisma's atomic increment operator creates race conditions when two scheduler instances run concurrently, causing one failure to be lost and weakening the delete after two failures logic

The Twilio provider API call and database persistence are in a single try-catch, so if Twilio accepts the SMS but the database update fails, the error is treated as a send failure causing duplicate SMS on retry
After multiple database failures, the reminder row may be deleted leaving orphaned jobs on Twilio with no database reference
The retryCount branch in the OR clause is not scoped to SMS, so it will delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method/scheduledDate, potentially removing other reminder types
retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 is not an atomic update and can lose increments if multiple schedulers/cron invocations overlap - should use Prisma's atomic increment via { increment: 1 }
Same non-atomic increment issue exists in another location - should use atomic increment to avoid lost updates if the job runs concurrently

ours.body: The `Caching` describe block was removed, but `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still memoize into `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts:83-95). others.text: Org-scope assertion is order-dependent even though the service fetches team/member IDs without orderBy, so the test can fail nondeterministically on valid SQL

(e.g. teamIds / uniqueUserIds) come from DB queries without explicit ordering, so the bound array order and resulting Prisma.sql shape may be non-deterministic, making SQL-fragment equality assertions brittle and causing inconsistent condition caching across identical inputs

This causes personal bookings (`isTeamBooking = false`) from members who are directly in the org to be missing from org-scope insights.
